__baseline_prompt__.text: A photographic scene of active investigation at the waterfront ticket booth after the last ferry has departed: an investigator is seeking information, seeking information about a case from the remaining ticket attendant. The empty boarding approach and the quiet water beyond the booth give the encounter its late, narrowing opportunity. The investigator's visible facial appearance follows the supplied reference, including its rounded facial outline, large dark eyes, fine straight brows and soft lips; her hair follows the reference's dark chin-length bob with wispy separated fringe. Her attentive presence is quietly compelling, absorbed in the answer. The photograph catches the precise instant when recognition turns into a usable location. Her anatomical left hand supports the portrait photograph upright for the attendant to see. The portrait presents one person's face. Her anatomical right hand holds the pen over an open notebook. The investigator grips the pen in her anatomical right hand with its nib suspended above the notebook page. A clear strip of air separates the nib from the paper as her recording pauses. The pen has a continuous narrow barrel and a clearly visible pointed nib. The notebook already contains a few short handwritten lines, while the held photograph remains upright and separate from both notebook and map. The attendant answers by pointing to a local map. The attendant's index fingertip touches the printed pier endpoint. The investigator's eyes are directed down to that same fingertip and pier endpoint. Her chin tilts toward the map, making the downward eye direction readable. The local map depicts a single narrow pier projecting from a curved shoreline into blue water, ending in a small square landing; the fingertip is planted on this outer landing. The map's broad shoreline, narrow pier neck and terminal landing remain visible around the contact. The attendant's face and slight speaking mouth support the explanation. The investigator occupies frame left, her torso nearly frontal: her left-hand photograph appears at screen-right beside her chest, and her right-hand pen and notebook appear at screen-left below it. Her separate forearms stay traceable to their corresponding shoulders. The attendant occupies frame right and reaches toward the map in the central foreground. The notebook rests on the near counter ledge, and the map is inclined on a shallow board beyond it, separating their planes. View from inside the booth, slightly above counter height and diagonally across the counter, with both faces, the two investigator hands, pen gap and map contact readable together. A diffused work lamp lights the faces, hands and pale paper against the cooler harbor dusk. Moderately deep focus joins the investigator's lowered eyes to the decisive counter details while the empty boarding approach remains recognizable behind her.
